plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with SVA for suspected batch
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 6 treated vs 6 control human kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (12000 genes, Salmon gene-level counts), with no recorded processing batch, but the PCA shows two clusters of six that cross-cut condition rather than follow it — a signature of an unrecorded technical or biological covariate (extraction date, dissection batch, RIN, etc.) rather than of the treatment itself. Ignoring this structure risks two failure modes: if the two clusters are ignored, the batch axis inflates test statistics and the differential expression call becomes a battery of false positives; if the clusters are naively 'corrected out' by subtracting them from the counts before testing, any component of the true treated-vs-control effect that happens to correlate with the cluster split is removed along with the noise, and the downstream test reports confidence the data does not support. The correct path (per grounded rule R-0025/R-0068) is: first look for a stated technical explanation for the two clusters using library size, mapping metrics and metadata; if none exists, estimate surrogate variables directly from the counts with sva (leaving the counts themselves untouched) and add those surrogate variables into the DESeq2 design formula alongside the condition term. The differential expression test then runs on the raw counts under design ~SV1+...+condition, so it estimates the treatment effect adjusted for the confounding axis instead of laundering it away first. Outputs are the Wald test with apeglm-shrunk log2 fold changes, BH-adjusted p-values with a p-value-histogram diagnostic (since a suspected, unmodeled batch is exactly the situation where a clean-looking histogram is not trustworthy), a robustness cross-check against edgeR quasi-likelihood, and fgsea preranked enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets, with all findings tied back to the actual gene identifiers, adjusted p-value cutoff (0.05) and the number of surrogate variables used.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size, colored by condition and by the two PCA clusters as a candidate surrogate/batch axis
keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (smallest group size)
sva-estimated surrogate variables added as covariates to ~SV1+...+condition, condition releveled to control as reference

DESeq2 Wald test on design ~SVs+condition, treated vs control; also fit edgeR QL as a second method for robustness overlap; keep flagged outlier sample and rely on DESeq2 Cook's-distance handling rather than silent removal
apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg on Wald p-values with independent filtering, alpha=0.05; inspect p-value histogram pre- and post-SV-adjustment, re-estimate null with fdrtool if histogram remains irregular
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome as a second collection

Report with QC diagnostics, design rationale (SVA to address the two suspected clusters), DE tables (shrunken + unshrunken LFC), MA/dispersion plots, enrichment tables with leading edges, DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap, sensitivity note on outlier sample
